question: The Indian who won the United Nations Sasakawa Award 2025 for Disaster Risk Reduction is popularly known as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclone Man of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sasakawa Award for Disaster Risk Reduction** is a prestigious recognition granted by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) to individuals and organizations for their outstanding contributions to disaster risk management and mitigation efforts globally.
 
• **Mritunjay Mohapatra**, popularly known as the **Cyclone Man of India**, is associated with accurate predictions and effective disaster risk reduction strategies, particularly in the context of cyclonic storms in the Indian region.
 
• He serves as the **Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, which plays a crucial role in forecasting and issuing early warnings for cyclones, saving countless lives.
 
• Mohapatra’s work in improving cyclone forecasting systems, including the use of advanced technology and satellite data, has earned him significant recognition in disaster risk reduction on both national and international levels.
 
• The Sasakawa Award 2025 highlights his contributions to disaster preparedness, mitigation, and climate resilience, showcasing India’s advancements in weather forecasting and disaster management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India Meteorological Department (IMD):**

 
 
• The IMD was established in **1875**, making it one of the oldest meteorological organizations globally.
 
• It is headquartered in **New Delhi** and functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India.
 
• The IMD specializes in weather forecasting, cyclone tracking, monsoon prediction, and disaster management, using state-of-the-art technologies such as Doppler radar systems and satellite data.
 
 
 
• **Cyclones in India:**
 
 
• India is vulnerable to tropical cyclones due to its extensive coastline spanning over **7,500 km**.
 
• Most cyclones affecting India originate in the **Bay of Bengal**, and states like Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal experience significant impacts.
 
• IMD plays a pivotal role in issuing warnings and minimizing the loss of life and property during cyclonic events.
 
 
 
• **Sasakawa Award:**
 
 
• Established in **1986**, the Sasakawa Award is administered by UNDRR and supported by the Nippon Foundation of Japan.
 
• The award recognizes individuals, organizations, and initiatives that demonstrate exemplary efforts in disaster risk reduction and resilience building.
 
• Recipients of the award are chosen based on their innovative approaches, community engagement, and measurable impact in disaster preparedness.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements of Mritunjay Mohapatra:**
 
 
• As the **Cyclone Man of India**, Mohapatra has enhanced IMD’s capabilities in tracking and predicting cyclones with precision.
 
• His leadership has contributed to minimizing the loss of life during cyclonic events through timely forecasts and effective communication strategies.
 
• He has been instrumental in promoting awareness about disaster preparedness and building resilience within vulnerable communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Advancements in Cyclone Forecasting:**

 
 
• The IMD uses advanced tools such as **Global Forecasting Systems (GFS)**, **Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF)** models, and **Dynamical Ocean Atmospheric Model (DOAM)** for accurate cyclone predictions.
 
• Doppler Weather Radars installed across coastal regions of India help in real-time monitoring of cyclonic storms.
 
• Satellite systems like **INSAT-3D** and **INSAT-3DR** contribute to enhanced forecasting capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Community-Based Disaster Preparedness:**
 
 
• Mohapatra’s efforts emphasize the importance of engaging local communities in disaster risk reduction.
 
• Training programs and awareness campaigns conducted by IMD have empowered people to respond effectively to cyclonic warnings.
 
• Collaborations with state governments and NGOs have strengthened India’s disaster management framework.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Mritunjay Mohapatra’s contributions have earned him global recognition, making India a leader in disaster risk reduction.
 
• His achievements align with the goals of the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030)**, which emphasizes reducing disaster risks through strategic planning and resilience building.
